text:
**Best slim pick: Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim), $54.99.** [Buy at Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank)

- **Size:** Anker lists it at 0.34 in (8.6 mm) thick and 4.3 oz (122 g).
- **Charging:** It has 5,000mAh and Qi2 wireless charging up to 15W, which Anker lists for iPhone 12 through 17.
- **Real-world capacity:** Anker says a full charge delivers about 2,750–3,500mAh to your phone after losses. That's roughly half to two-thirds of an iPhone 17 charge. It's a top-up pack, not an all-day one.
- **Reviewer view:** 9to5Mac's [battery bank roundup](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/) names it the top slim pick. It says it's the closest match to Apple's design and runs cooler than competitors.
- **Recalls:** Anker's page doesn't mention a recall for this model. It does link to a general recalls page, so check that page if you buy.

**Other options, depending on what you need**
- **More capacity: UGREEN 10,000mAh, about $59.99.** It supports Qi2.2 at up to 25W, which works with iPhone 16 and later, including the 17. It also has 30W wired charging and a built-in USB-C cable. 9to5Mac says it's not as thin. I didn't get a direct product link for it.
- **Extra features: Belkin 25W 10,000mAh, about $99.99.** It has a kickstand, a capacity display, and a second magnetic ring on the back. 9to5Mac calls it a little chunky.
- **Cheapest: Baseus 5,000mAh, about $24.99.** It's slim, but 9to5Mac lists it at only 7.5W wireless with no Qi2, so it will charge an iPhone 17 more slowly. The reviewer also hasn't tested it personally.
- **Possible Anker rival: [LISEN P601](https://lisenintl.com/products/p601-magsafe-power-bank/).** It's a 5,000mAh, 15W Qi2 pack listed at 0.38 in thick. I only saw the listing, with no independent review, so treat it as unverified.

**What I couldn't check**
- The Android Central test of 2026 slim Qi2 banks (Baseus, TORRAS, INIU, ReelCharge) wouldn't load, so those brands aren't in my comparison.
- 9to5Mac doesn't give thickness or weight for any bank, so I can't compare sizes beyond Anker's own specs.
- The Baseus PicoGo AM52 deal in the results is a 10,000mAh, 45W model, so it isn't a slim pick. I also didn't verify that coupon.

If you want a bigger battery and don't mind some bulk, get the UGREEN. Otherwise the Anker Nano is the best slim choice.
